title: Festival of Remembrance
subtitle: Songs from across Latin America and Central America for remembering the people we have lost, from celebration to grief to gratitude.

tracks.style_note: A haunting Argentine canción telling the story of poet Alfonsina Storni, who died by suicide by walking into the sea in 1938. The song imagines her final journey with extraordinary tenderness, turning a tragic real-life death into a beautiful musical elegy.
A melancholic tango classic about the bitter-sweet pain of returning home, bearing the scars of time, loss, and lingering memories.
A delicate Samba masterpiece reflecting on heartbreak and mortality, where silence and fading roses speak of profound, unspoken grief.

Violeta Parra's extraordinary farewell to life, expressing gratitude for the senses, love, laughter, sorrow and everything that makes us human. Written shortly before her death, the song has acquired an especially poignant legacy. It is less about mourning the dead than celebrating the life they experienced and the memories they leave behind.
A tender Chilean angelito funeral song celebrating a child's soul ascending to heaven, transforming grief into pure spiritual light.
The iconic Cuban song, a fusion of bolero and Cuban 'son', that expresses deep sorrow over lost love and abandonment.
Translating to 'We Cannot Forget', this is an upbeat confrontation to loss and tragedy from the defiant Haitian Rasin band, who seamlessly blend Vodou-derived rhythms with rock and modern sounds.
A serene, spiritual dance dedicated to the Gede spirits of death and rebirth, using fluid Vodou rhythms to honour ancestral memory.

The haunting centrepiece of Mexico's Day of the Dead musical tradition. La Llorona, the Weeping Woman, is a legendary ghost condemned to wander in grief. This traditional Oaxacan song blends folklore, lost love and the pain of separation.
A stirring, brass-filled Oaxacan anthem calling for God's love to help the soul endure the grief of loss.
A life-affirming celebration of those who have passed, remembered through the November blooms of the emblem of Día de los Muertos, the Cempasúchil (the marigold flower).
Meaning “Remember Me” this tender ballad is a heartfelt plea to a loved one to keep memories alive even after separation or loss.
A whimsical, even joyous tribute to La Calaca, the skeleton symbol of Dia de los Muertos, embodying the idea that death is a joyful and equalizing force.
Las Chorizeras are the all-female, contemporary Mariachi fusion group, bringing this fresh, vibrant celebration of the little skulls and skeleton imagery associated with Día de Muertos.
A vibrant, gypsy-jazz-infused folk tune offering a wry, life-affirming reminder that death awaits us all, so we might as well live fully now.
At once deeply personal and communal, this 'Day of the Dead' funeral chant is a solemn offering of spiritual prayers for eternal rest and solace to grieving families.
